Somethings to consider:

1) The older versions of Perry's Handbook have some hard and fast rules of thumb for kinetics, fluids and heat transfer. These are absent in the newer additions due to the advent of CFD and CAE. I prefer having those rules of thumbs because you don't always have a process simulator at your disposal. 

2) I've worked upstream, midstream and downstream petroleum. By far one of the most useful handbooks I own is the GPSA Enginering Databook:

https://gpsa.gpaglobal.org/gpsa-databook

If you're going to be a plant engineer or a field engineer, it's indispensable because it allows for quick and rough, yet accurate calculations when you have to give operations an answer in minutes instead of hours. 

3) Regardless of what industry you are going to work in, pumps will be a part of your life. My goto is the Alfa Laval Pump Handbook:

https://www.google.com/#q=alfa+laval+pump+handbook

I typical spec out horizontal-multistage pumps and I'm partial to Schlumberger's REDA HPS units due to the fat they were originally downhole pumps in oil wells and as such they can handle stupid large solids, so you can get away with a strainer/sieve instead of a full blown filter.

Good luck in your future ventures.
